subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Fingerprint Recognition
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Fingerprint Recognition.

hook.text: Your fingerprint unlocks your phone in a second. That same fingerprint can identify you for life.

buildup.text: Fingerprint recognition matches the unique ridge patterns on your fingertips against a stored template.

discovery.text: Fingerprints have been used for identification since the 1890s. They were the first biometric identifier.

twist.text: Once your fingerprint is stolen from a database, you can't change it. It's compromised permanently.

climax.text: Fingerprints are convenient for unlocking phones — and permanent liabilities if the database is breached.

punchline.text: Convenient to use. Impossible to change if stolen.

quiz.question: Why is a fingerprint data breach more serious than a password breach?
options: Fingerprints cannot be changed or reset
Fingerprints are less unique than passwords
Passwords are stored more securely than fingerprints
